title: You Ain’t Nothin But a Postmark

sentences.en: In 1992, a historic election captivated the nation.
sentences.zh: 1992年，一场历史性的选举吸引了全国的目光。

sentences.en: The race pitted a young up-and-comer against an old guard establishment candidate.
sentences.zh: 这场竞选让一位年轻的后起之秀与一位老派的建制派候选人展开了角逐。

sentences.en: And I'm not talking about the 1992 presidential election
sentences.zh: 我指的并不是1992年的总统大选，

sentences.en: between Arkansas Governor Bill Clinton and the incumbent George H.W.
sentences.zh: 也就是阿肯色州州长比尔·克林顿与在任总统乔治·H·W·

sentences.en: Instead, this was the highly publicized race between young Elvis and old Elvis.
sentences.zh: 相反，这是一场广受关注的竞选，主角是年轻的猫王和年老的猫王。
特约记者盖比·布拉德报道。

sentences.zh: 猫王邮票的投票吸引了全国的注意力，

sentences.zh: 甚至还影响了1992年的总统大选。

sentences.zh: 当最终投票结束，每一张选票都被清点完毕时，

sentences.zh: 邮票从此被永远改变了。

sentences.zh: 当你寄信时，有很多邮票可供选择。

sentences.zh: 你可以走传统路线，使用美国国旗图案，

sentences.en: or you can choose a stamp that fits your personality.
sentences.zh: 或者选择一张符合你个性的邮票。

sentences.zh: 但这种百花齐放的邮票种类其实是相当新鲜的事物。

sentences.zh: 事实上，直到19世纪中期，我们才有了邮票。

sentences.en: In the early years of the post office,
mail was often sent cash on delivery, like a collect call.
sentences.zh: 邮件通常是货到付款，就像对方付费电话一样。

sentences.en: If someone sent you a letter,
you paid for it when you picked it up at the post office.
sentences.zh: 你得在去邮局取信时支付邮费。

sentences.en: and the system for calculating fees was complicated.
sentences.zh: 而且计算费用的系统非常复杂。

sentences.zh: 很难预知一封信最终要花多少钱。
实施标准化邮资费率后，

sentences.en: the cost to mail letters became more predictable and less expensive.
sentences.zh: 寄信的成本变得更可预测，也更便宜了。

sentences.en: Now a person could pay to send a letter in advance,
sentences.zh: 现在，寄信人可以预先支付邮费，

sentences.en: and the recipient could get it without a fee.
sentences.zh: 收件人无需付费即可收到信件。

sentences.en: A stamp was proof that a sender had paid for the mail.
sentences.zh: 邮票就是寄件人已支付邮费的证明。

sentences.en: issued its first national stamps in 1847,
sentences.zh: 在1847年发行了第一批全国性邮票，

sentences.zh: 发行了越来越多的邮票种类。

sentences.en: Stamps marked anniversaries, celebrated big events,

体制化的和爱国主义的。

sentences.en: Like paper currency or like a bond or something like that,
sentences.zh: 就像纸币、债券之类的东西一样，

sentences.en: it's meant to represent the country.
And so putting someone on a stamp is essentially a government endorsement.
sentences.zh: 所以把某人印在邮票上，本质上就是一种政府背书。

sentences.zh: 但邮局也有动力去设计新颖的邮票。

sentences.zh: 因为随着第一批邮票的出现，第一批集邮者也随之诞生了。

sentences.zh: 他们为邮政服务提供了独特的价值。
